meta.description: MCP tools for provider/model discovery and one-shot CLI agent invocation, following the tool_groups pattern

phases.name: Settings & Registration Scaffolding
phases.description: Add the providers tool group to the registration system and settings defaults. No tools yet — just the scaffolding so the group is recognized and can be enabled/disabled.

tasks.name: Add providers to settings.json
tasks.description: Add tools.providers section to settings.json with enabled: true and default_timeout: 120

tasks.name: Create providers_tools.py with empty register()
tasks.description: Create vista/tool_groups/providers_tools.py with a register(mcp, settings) function that registers no tools yet (just logs). Follow the pattern of ralph_tools.py.

acceptanceCriteria: MCP server starts without errors with providers tool group enabled
Server log shows 'Registered tool group: providers' at startup
Disabling tools.providers.enabled = false skips registration

phases.name: list_providers MCP Tool
phases.description: Implement the list_providers tool that returns all enabled providers with live-discovered models and metadata. Reuses existing get_ralph_providers() infrastructure.

tasks.name: Implement list_providers tool
tasks.description: Add @mcp.tool() async def list_providers() that calls get_ralph_providers() and returns JSON with 'providers' key (no ralph-specific defaults/summarizer). Handle errors with JSON error response matching teams/ralph pattern.

tasks.name: Unit tests for list_providers
tasks.description: Test: returns correct structure, respects enabled/disabled providers, handles missing CLI gracefully, handles missing ralph settings, includes model metadata when present.

acceptanceCriteria: list_providers returns JSON with providers array
Each provider has name, display_name, and models with metadata
Only enabled providers appear
Missing CLI binary results in provider with empty models array (not error)
All unit tests pass

phases.name: invoke_provider MCP Tool
phases.description: Implement the invoke_provider tool that sends a prompt to a CLI agent via subprocess and returns the response. Uses existing _run_cli_with_timeout() and get_chat_cmd() infrastructure.

tasks.name: Create invoke_provider helper function
tasks.description: Create a _invoke_cli_provider(provider_name, model, prompt, timeout) function in providers_tools.py that: 1) looks up provider via get_provider_by_name(), 2) validates model availability, 3) gets CLI command via get_chat_cmd(), 4) spawns subprocess with stdin pipe, 5) handles timeout with process-tree kill, 6) returns stdout or error. Reuse _run_cli_with_timeout() patterns for Windows compat (CREATE_NO_WINDOW, .cmd handling, taskkill).

tasks.name: Implement invoke_provider tool
tasks.description: Add @mcp.tool() async def invoke_provider(provider, model, prompt, timeout) that calls _invoke_cli_provider() and returns response text on success or JSON error on failure. Default timeout from settings.tools.providers.default_timeout.

tasks.name: Unit tests for invoke_provider
tasks.description: Test with mocked subprocess: success case, timeout case, non-zero exit, unknown provider, disabled provider, missing binary, unavailable model, empty response, special characters in prompt. Verify stdin piping (not CLI args).

acceptanceCriteria: invoke_provider returns raw response text on success
invoke_provider returns JSON error for all error cases
Prompt is piped via stdin, not CLI arguments
Timeout kills process tree (taskkill /T /F on Windows)
CREATE_NO_WINDOW flag set on Windows
.cmd/.bat wrappers handled with cmd.exe /c prefix
All unit tests pass

phases.name: Provider Base Class Documentation
phases.description: Document the Provider base class contract: required vs optional methods, how to add a new provider, and the get_spawn_info() forward-looking method for teams integration.

tasks.name: Add contract documentation to Provider class
tasks.description: Add comprehensive docstring to Provider base class categorizing methods as required (get_models, get_chat_cmd, get_invocation) vs optional (get_summarizer_command, get_persistent_cmd, parse_stream_event, supports_streaming, stdin_pipe). Add get_summarizer_command() fallback to get_chat_cmd() in base class.

tasks.name: Add get_spawn_info() method
tasks.description: Add get_spawn_info() -> dict to Provider base class returning {'binary': self.name, 'spawn_style': 'generic-cli', 'supports_interactive': False}. Override in ClaudeProvider (spawn_style='claude-native', supports_interactive=True) and OpenCodeProvider (spawn_style='opencode-api'). This is forward-looking for teams spawner integration.

tasks.name: Unit tests for provider contract
tasks.description: Test: minimal subclass with only required methods works. Test: get_summarizer_command() fallback. Test: get_spawn_info() defaults and overrides.

acceptanceCriteria: Provider docstring clearly documents required vs optional methods
get_summarizer_command() falls back to get_chat_cmd() in base class
get_spawn_info() returns sensible defaults
ClaudeProvider and OpenCodeProvider override get_spawn_info()
All unit tests pass

phases.name: Integration Testing & Verification
phases.description: End-to-end testing with real CLI providers to verify the full workflow: discovery -> invoke -> verify response.

tasks.name: Integration test: list_providers with real Claude
tasks.description: Test that list_providers returns claude with opus/sonnet/haiku models when Claude CLI is installed.

tasks.name: Integration test: invoke_provider with real Claude
tasks.description: Test invoke_provider('claude', 'haiku', 'Say hello in one word') returns non-empty response.

tasks.name: Integration test: discovery -> invoke workflow
tasks.description: Call list_providers, pick first provider and model, call invoke_provider with a simple prompt, verify response.

tasks.name: Verify coexistence with teams and ralph tools
tasks.description: Enable all three tool groups simultaneously, verify all tools register without conflicts, verify each group works independently.

acceptanceCriteria: list_providers returns real provider data with installed CLIs
invoke_provider returns real responses from Claude CLI
All three tool groups coexist without naming conflicts
Full discovery -> invoke workflow works end-to-end
